facts.text: In 1862 Andrew Gardener claimed 160 acres of beachfront property and built the Zephyr Cove House inn, marking the town's founding.
The community was named Zephyr Cove after the Washoe word for the gentle westerly winds that sweep the area each afternoon.
Before settlers arrived, the Washoe people inhabited the Zephyr Cove area, viewing Lake Tahoe as the spiritual center of their world.
The 1950s saw a surge of automobile tourists, peaking during the 1960 Winter Olympics in nearby Squaw Valley, which spurred lakeshore development in Zephyr Cove.
The M.S. Dixie II, a custom‑built paddlewheeler launched in 1994, was assembled at Zephyr Cove and continues the lake’s cruise tradition.
Zephyr Cove hosts a branch of the Douglas County Public Library, offering residents access to regional books and community programs.
